panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial T1 MRI without contrast showing left lacrimal gland enlargement attributed to IgG4-RD in caption and IgG4-RD case report title; infraorbital nerve findings are perineural spread variant. B: Axial fat-saturated T1 MRI with contrast at same level showing left lacrimal gland enlargement and bilateral infraorbital nerve enhancement attributed to IgG4-RD; perineural extension is less common variant.
panels.attribution_text: Sirvisetty et al. Perineural Spread of Orbital Immunoglobulin G4-Related Disease: A Case Report.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.77790. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Axial MRI scans of orbits with and without contrast Axial T1 weighted MR image without contrast (A) and axial fat-saturated T1 weighted MR image at the same level with contrast (B). There is enlargement with thickening of the left lacrimal gland (yellow oval) related to IgG4-RD. Furthermore, there is thickening with an enhancement of the infraorbital nerves bilaterally within the infraorbital nerve canal (orange arrows), pterygopalatine fossa (blue arrow), and entering the foramen rotundum (red arrows). On the right side, infraorbital nerve enhancement extends through the foramen rotundum into the expected location of Meckel's cave. IgG4-RD - immunoglobulin G4-related disease
in_text_mentions: Coronal MRI scans of the orbits with and without contrast demonstrate bilateral enlargement of the extraocular muscles, orbital nerves, and peri-ophthalmitis (Figures 1A-B). Axial MRI scans of the orbits with and without contrast demonstrate infiltrative enlargement of the left lacrimal gland and perineural extension of disease along the infraorbital nerves (Figures 2A-B). The differential diagnosis includes IgG4-related disease, sarcoidosis, lymphoma, atypical thyroid ophthalmopathy, and granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

in_text_mentions: A CT-guided biopsy of the right pleural mass was obtained, and the results showed xanthogranulomatous inflammation with immunohistochemistry revealing an increase in IgG4-positive plasma cells (Figure 4). The culture was also sent out and came back negative. IgG4 serological testing showed IgG4 levels of 187 mg/dL. Due to the patient's comorbidities and overall clinical condition, the multidisciplinary managing team, including thoracic surgery, hepatobiliary, and immunology specialists, opted against any intervention for the patient.

in_text_mentions: These findings prompted the decision to perform a kidney biopsy, especially after an ultrasound revealed normal-sized kidneys (125 and 130 mm in diameter) with reasonable cortical thickness and corticomedullary differentiation. The kidney biopsy showed lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate (70%), extensive storiform fibrosis, and IgG4 staining (>10 cells per high-power field), with preserved glomeruli and vessels (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E of resected pericardium from case of IgG4-related disease manifested as constrictive pericarditis; caption states partial lymphocyte infiltration and prominent fibrosis, supporting IgG4-related lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in pericardial tissue. B: Higher magnification H&E of same resected pericardium showing lymphocyte infiltration and fibrosis, consistent with IgG4-related disease pericardial involvement. C: IgG immunostaining of resected pericardium with increased IgG4-positive plasma cells; in-text 70 cells per HPF and elevated IgG4/IgG ratio and serum IgG4 679 mg/dL support definitive IgG4-related disease. D: IgG4 immunostaining of resected pericardium showing substantial increase in IgG4-positive plasma cells, diagnostic of IgG4-related constrictive pericarditis per article title and criteria.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real patient chest CT shows pleural nodule attributed to IgG4-related disease per caption and article title, but no vocabulary finding_key covers lung/pleural nodule; per rule 6 excluded when no finding can be named, proposed as pleural nodule. B: Abdominal CT shows periaortitis / infrarenal periaortic soft-tissue densification in Patient 2 with elevated IgG4 and article diagnosis of lung and pleural IgG4-related disease, matching periaortic retroperitoneal mass vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Diz-Lopes et al. Lung and Pleural Immunoglobulin G4-Related Disease: Two Contrasting Case Reports.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.35439. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Computed tomography (CT) scan of Patient 2. (A) Chest CT scan revealing one of the newly identified pleural nodules on the left inferior lobe (red arrow). (B) Abdominal CT scan with periaortitis (densification of the fat adjacent to the infrarenal aorta, yellow arrow).
in_text_mentions: ut sustained elevation of CRP (400 to 200 mg/L) and ESR (128 mm/h). Other laboratory blood tests were requested, showing normocytic normochromic anemia, positive ANA titers (1/100) in a speckled pattern with negativity for other autoantibodies, normal serum levels of complement proteins, normal serum levels of total IgG, and elevation of IgG4 serum levels (IgG4: 201 mg/dL, reference range: 8-140 mg/dL). A whole-body CT scan showed two new pleural nodules and densification of the fat adjacent to the infrarenal aorta with a longitudinal extension of 47 mm on a circumferential pattern (Figure 4).
